items.evidence: AC#1 passes. It uses toStrictEqual on the whole result and checks the spy input (hero, 3 flop cards, 3 ranges of 1081 with no dead cards). It fails under the >= to > mutation. Holdout: on 112 real facing-bet spots (3 to 10 seats, flop/turn/river), an injected equity equal to the required % (and one just under the rounding point, so it rounds up to it) always gave call with equityPct = requiredEquityPct.

AC#2 passes (fold, pot-odds-fold, 16.6 vs 16.7, move {seat 3, fold}). Holdout: on every real facing-bet spot, an injected equity 0.1 points below required, or just below the half-up rounding point, gave fold / pot-odds-fold.

AC#3 property passes (40 runs, seed 7303) and fails when check-free is disabled. Interpretation: the property plays non-fold actions to a random postflop decision (stopAt 0..11), not only the first one. With 6 live players and stacks of 160 it reaches flop and turn decisions but never the river, and the fc.pre discard never triggers. That is wider than the spec's literal 'first decision' (always a flop decision when there are no folds) but does not reach the river, so the river is not covered by this property (J-1-01, LOW). Holdout covers the gap: 160 real random hands with folds allowed, 3 to 10 seats (91 flop, 37 turn, 32 river spots; 138 with folded seats; 18 river multiway with folded seats; 22 heads-up). Every result had a legal move of type action, a ruleId in POSTFLOP_RULE_IDS, percentages in [0,100] with one decimal, and the rule matched the rounded comparison. No bet or raise was ever recommended.

AC#4 passes (check, check-free, required 0, callAmount 0, pot 16, equity in (0,100), move {seat 3, check}; injected 0.01 still checks). It fails when check-free is disabled. Holdout: 48 real free-check spots all gave check-free; injected equity 0, 0.001 and 1 all gave check.

AC#5 passes, and ruleProblems gives the three specified messages for a removed describe, a missing engine id and an extra doc id. It fails when a fourth id is added to POSTFLOP_RULE_IDS. Holdout: the doc's ### Rule headings equal POSTFLOP_RULE_IDS in order, and each id has a describe('rule <id>' block in postflop.test.ts.

AC#6 passes: 20-run permutations on the flop and turn spots, turn pot 24 / call 8 / 25%, and a hero-card control. Holdout: 120 permutations over 40 real spots, including river multiway with folded seats and 10-seat tables. All other hole cards, burns and undealt cards were shuffled and the same actions replayed; the board was unchanged and every result deep-strict-equal to the original.

The unit describes for check-free, pot-odds-call (including the 0.1665 rounds-to-call case added in the fix) and pot-odds-fold pass, and the toPct examples pass. The pot-odds-call test fails under both the >= to > and the unrounded-comparison mutations. Holdout: toPct is half-up correct at all 1000 boundaries (n+0.5)/1000, just below them, and at n/1000. toPct(call/(pot+call)) equals exact integer half-up rounding for calls 1..16 and pots 1..2000.

The inputs unit test passes: 1081/1035/990 ascending ranges, river with 2 opponents after seat 6 folds, HU river exact, repeat call strict-equal. It fails when folded players are counted. Holdout, independent of the code: pot = sum of totalContribution, callAmount = currentBet - streetContribution, opponents = live non-hero count. All 160 random spots matched, as did a 10-seat flop with 9 opponents (pot 44). Equity computed from my own input (full 1326-combo ranges) matched equityPct and equityMethod on all 160 spots. A brute-force evaluator-based exact equity matched computeEquity to 1e-9 on 11 exact river/turn spots. Determinism: a repeat call deep-equals the first on every spot. The view is not mutated.

The API unit test passes. Holdout: preflop RangeError 'Postflop advice needs a flop, turn or river view, got preflop'; 'Seat 1 is not to act' (also through recommend()); showdown message through recommend(); 'No legal call for seat 3'; 'No legal fold for seat 3'. recommend(preflop view) deep-equals recommendPreflop with basis 'chart'. recommend(postflop view) deep-equals recommendPostflop on all 160 spots, and options.equity passes through recommend().

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: the AC#3 'any postflop decision' property reaches river decisions, and its discard path for hands that end early can actually run. Actual: with folds excluded, 6 live players, 160 stacks and stopAt <= 11, every run stops on a flop or turn decision, and fc.pre never discards. River behaviour is covered elsewhere: the SPEC-08 unit test, and in judge checks, real random river spots with folded seats, all correct.
findings.fix: Optional: widen the property's stop range, or allow folds, so some runs reach a river decision.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected (A-4): the 1e-9 nudge in toPct matters for inputs like 0.1665. Actual: removing the nudge changes no observed output. The specified examples and all n/1000 and (n+0.5)/1000 boundaries round the same with or without it, so no test pins it. Behaviour is correct either way.
findings.fix: None required; optionally pin an input where the nudge changes the result, or drop the rationale.

summary: All 15 SPEC items PASS. The full suite is green (151 passed, 1 pre-existing skip), lint and typecheck are clean, the new modules have 100% coverage, real-target perf is within budget (5.0/12.9/71.6 ms), the 10,000-hand playtest has 0 violations, and CI run 44376112966 on b4840a5 succeeded. Holdout: 3133 checks on 160 real engine spots (3 to 10 seats, flop/turn/river, folded seats, heads-up) against independent pot, call, opponent, required-equity and rounding oracles, plus a brute-force exact equity oracle; 120 hidden-card permutations; determinism; recommend() dispatch; error messages; doc vs code. All pass. Integrity is clean, and the spec's mutation probes are all caught. On AC#3: the builder plays to a random postflop decision rather than only the first. That is wider than the spec's wording but never reaches the river (LOW, covered elsewhere). No blocking findings.
